In 2004 an episode of _Mythbusters_ referenced the accident and Betty Lou Oliver's survival when testing the myth that jumping just before a falling elevator crashes would save your life.
They ruled this myth "Busted", as a human's jumping power (approximately 2-3 mph/3-5 kph) cannot cancel out the falling velocity of an elevator (approximately 53 mph/85 kph).

The program speculated that Oliver's survival in 1945 was due to the tight elevator shaft creating an air cushion which, combined with the spring action from a slack elevator cable, could have slowed the elevator to a survivable speed.
